title: Sounds in Words
bigQuestion: What do you hear inside a word?

story.title: I Spy With My Ears
story.kicker: The clue is not a color. The clue is a sound.
paragraphs: It is rug time in Ms. Ortiz's class. She says, "Let's play I Spy. But today the clue is a sound." The kids lean in. Ms. Ortiz says, "I spy something that starts with /b/." She says the sound, not the letter. Just /b/, like a bubble popping.

Hands go up. "Ball!" says Devon. Ms. Ortiz shakes her head. "Good try. Ball does start with /b/. But I do not see a ball." Kids look around the room. There is a clock. There is a door. There is a book.

Priya says the word slowly. "Buh... book. Book starts with /b/!" Ms. Ortiz smiles. "Yes! The first sound in book is /b/." Now it is Priya's turn. She looks around. She says, "I spy something that starts with /d/."
Devon says, "Door!" He is right. Every word in the room has a first sound. Clock. Rug. Window. Once you hear the first sound, you can play this game anywhere.
story.think: Look around your room. Pick one thing. What sound does its name start with?

lessons.title: Words Are Made of Sounds
lessons.mainIdea: Every word is made of small sounds put together.
reading: Say the word cat. Now say it very slowly. Stretch it out. Do you hear it? C... a... t. Cat is not one sound. Cat is three sounds. They are stuck together.
Every word is like this. A *word* is a set of *sounds* said in a row. Say sun slowly. S... u... n. Three sounds. Say go slowly. G... o. Two sounds.
Your ears can pull a word apart. Your mouth can say each piece. This is a big skill. When you hear the sounds, you are ready to read them.

words.d: a set of sounds said together that means something
one small piece of a word that you hear

look.title: How Many Sounds?
look.prompt: Say jump slowly. Can you hear all four sounds?

check.q: How many sounds are in the word cat?
check.why: Say it slowly: c... a... t. That is three sounds stuck together.

check.q: What is a word made of?
check.why: A word is a set of sounds said together. Cat has three of them.

check.q: How can you hear the sounds in a word?
check.why: When you say a word slowly, you can hear each piece.

lessons.title: The First Sound
lessons.mainIdea: The first sound is the sound you hear at the start of a word.
reading: Say mom. What sound comes out first? /m/. Your lips press together. That is the *first sound*. Now say dog. The first sound is /d/. Your tongue taps the top of your mouth.
The first sound is the start of the word. It is the sound you hear before all the others. Say sun. /s/ comes first. Say fish. /f/ comes first.
Play a game. Say your name slowly. What sound comes first? Now say a friend's name. Do they start the same? Maria and Max both start with /m/.

words.d: the sound at the very start of a word

look.title: Two Bags of Toys
look.text: Look at two bags. One bag is for /b/ things. One bag is for /s/ things. Here are the toys: a ball, a sock, a bear, a spoon, a boat. Say each one slowly. Listen for the first sound. Then drop it in the right bag.
look.prompt: Which toys go in the /b/ bag? How do you know?

check.q: What is the first sound in dog?
check.why: Say dog slowly. The sound at the very start is /d/.

check.q: Which word starts with /s/?
check.why: Sock starts with /s/. Bear starts with /b/. Fish starts with /f/.

check.q: Where do you hear the first sound?
choices: At the end of a word
In the middle of a word
At the start of a word
check.why: The first sound is the very start. In mom, it is /m/.

lessons.title: Last Sound, Middle Sound
lessons.mainIdea: Words have a last sound and a middle sound too.
reading: Say bus. Say it slowly. B... u... s. The *last sound* is /s/. It is the sound at the end. Say cup. The last sound is /p/. Your lips pop.
Now find the *middle sound*. Say cat slowly. C... a... t. The middle sound is /a/. It sits between /c/ and /t/. Say pig. The middle sound is /i/.
The middle sound is the hard one. It is short. It goes by fast. So stretch the word out. Say it like a slow song. Caaaat. Now you can hear the /a/.

words.d: the sound at the very end of a word
the sound between the first sound and the last sound

look.title: Cat, Cot, Cut
look.text: Say these three words slowly. Cat. Cot. Cut. They all start with /c/. They all end with /t/. But they are not the same word. Listen to the middle. Cat has /a/. Cot has /o/. Cut has /u/. The middle sound changes everything.
look.prompt: Which sound is different in cat, cot and cut?

check.q: What is the last sound in bus?
check.why: Say bus slowly. The sound at the end is /s/.

check.q: What is the middle sound in cat?
check.why: C... a... t. The /a/ sits in the middle.

check.q: Why is the middle sound hard to hear?
check.why: The middle sound is short. Stretching the word helps you hear it.

lessons.title: Words That Rhyme
lessons.mainIdea: Words rhyme when their ends sound the same.
reading: Say cat. Say hat. Listen to the ends. C-at. H-at. Both end with -at. Cat and hat *rhyme*. Two words rhyme when their ends sound the same.
Try more. Dog and log. Sun and fun. Bed and red. The first sound is different. The rest of the word matches. That is why they sound like a pair.
Rhymes are all over songs and poems. Twinkle, twinkle, little star. How I wonder what you are. Star and are rhyme. Your ears already know this game.

words.d: when two words end with the same sound, like cat and hat

look.title: A Rhyme You Can Say
look.text: Ten little ducks sat in the sun. One little duck went off to run. Nine little ducks said, "That was fun!"
look.prompt: Which three words rhyme? Say them out loud.

check.q: Which word rhymes with cat?
check.why: Cat and hat both end with -at. Their ends sound the same.

check.q: When do two words rhyme?
choices: When their ends sound the same
check.why: Rhymes match at the end. Sun and fun both end with -un.

check.q: Sun and fun rhyme. Which part is different?
check.why: Sun starts with /s/. Fun starts with /f/. The rest is the same.

lessons.title: Clap the Parts
lessons.mainIdea: You can clap the beats in a word to count its parts.
reading: Say apple. Clap as you say it. Ap-ple. Two claps. Now say cat. One clap. Say banana. Ba-na-na. Three claps. Each clap is one *syllable*. A syllable is one beat of a word.
Try your name. Say it and clap. Sam gets one clap. Ma-ri-a gets three claps. Long names get more claps. Short names get one.
Put your hand under your chin. Say elephant. El-e-phant. Your chin drops three times. That is three syllables. Your chin can count for you.

words.d: one beat in a word; apple has two

look.title: Clap and Count
look.prompt: Which food name has the most beats? Clap it out.

check.q: How many claps does apple get?
check.why: Ap-ple. Two beats, so two claps.

check.q: What is a syllable?
choices: The first sound of a word
check.why: A syllable is one beat. Banana has three beats.

check.q: Your chin drops three times when you say a word. How many syllables is that?
check.why: Your chin drops once for each beat. Three drops means three syllables.

lessons.title: Blend the Sounds
lessons.mainIdea: Put sounds together in a row and they make a word.
reading: Listen. /m/... /a/... /p/. Three sounds, one at a time. Now say them fast. Push them together. Map! You just made a word. This is called *blending*.
Blending is like gluing beads on a string. Each sound is a bead. Say them close together. /s/ /u/ /n/. Sun. /d/ /o/ /g/. Dog.
Go slow at first. Say the first sound. Hold it. Slide into the next one. Sssuuunnn. Then say it fast. Sun. Readers do this all day long.

words.d: saying sounds together fast so they make a word

look.title: The Robot Talks
look.text: A toy robot says words in pieces. It says, "/p/... /i/... /g/." Its friend Lena hears the sounds. She pushes them together in her head. She says, "Pig!" The robot beeps. It says, "/h/... /a/... /t/." Lena smiles. She knows this one too.
look.prompt: What word did the robot say the second time?

check.q: What is blending?
choices: Putting sounds together to make a word
Clapping the beats of a word
check.why: Blending pushes sounds together. /m/ /a/ /p/ becomes map.

check.q: Blend these sounds: /s/ /u/ /n/. What word is it?
check.why: Say the sounds fast and close. They make the word sun.

check.q: What should you do when blending is hard?
choices: Go slow and hold each sound
check.why: Slow blending works. Hold the first sound and slide to the next.

lessons.title: Take a Word Apart
lessons.mainIdea: You can break a word into its sounds, one at a time.
reading: Blending puts sounds together. Now go the other way. Say the word hop. Pull it apart. /h/... /o/... /p/. You broke hop into three sounds. That is *taking apart*.
Use your fingers. Say sit. Hold up one finger for each sound. /s/ is one. /i/ is two. /t/ is three. Three fingers. Three sounds.
This helps you spell. To write a word, you need its sounds. Say the word. Take it apart. Then write one letter for each sound you hear.

words.d: saying each sound in a word one at a time

look.title: Fingers Up
look.text: Jamal wants to write the word bug. He says it slowly. He puts up one finger. /b/. Two fingers. /u/. Three fingers. /g/. Now he has three fingers up. He knows bug has three sounds. He can write one letter for each one.
look.prompt: Why does Jamal hold up his fingers?

check.q: Take apart the word hop. What are the sounds?
check.why: Hop has three sounds in this order: /h/, /o/, /p/.

check.q: How many fingers do you hold up for sit?
check.why: Sit has three sounds: /s/, /i/, /t/. One finger for each.

check.q: How does taking a word apart help you?
choices: It helps you spell the word
check.why: When you hear each sound, you can write a letter for each one.

lessons.title: Change One Sound
lessons.mainIdea: Change one sound in a word and you get a new word.
reading: Say cat. Now take off the /c/. Put /h/ in its place. Hat! Take off the /h/. Put on /b/. Bat! You changed one sound. You made a new word each time.
You can change the end too. Say cat. Take off the /t/. Put on /p/. Cap! You can change the middle. Cat. Cot. Cut. One small change makes a whole new word.
This is a *word game* you can play anywhere. Start with pin. Change one sound. Pan. Change one more. Man. Keep going. How far can you get?

words.d: a game where you play with the sounds in words

look.title: The Word Ladder
look.text: Look at the word ladder. On the first step is the word cat. Change one sound. Step up to hat. Change one sound. Step up to hot. Change one sound. Step up to pot. Each step is a new word. Each step is only one sound away from the last one.
look.prompt: Which sound changed to go from hat to hot?

check.q: Change the /c/ in cat to /h/. What word do you get?
check.why: Take off /c/ and put on /h/. C-at becomes h-at, hat.

check.q: Cat becomes cap. Which sound changed?
check.why: The /t/ at the end became /p/. The first and middle sounds stayed.

check.q: What happens when you change one sound in a word?
check.why: One sound change makes a new word. Pin becomes pan.

review.q: What is a word made of?
review.why: Every word is a set of sounds put together. Cat has three.

review.q: What is the first sound in sun?
review.why: Say sun slowly. The sound at the very start is /s/.
Dog and log both end with -og. Their ends sound the same.

review.q: How many claps does banana get?
review.why: Ba-na-na. Three beats, so three claps.
Say the sounds fast and close together. They make dog.

review.q: Change the /p/ in pin to /f/. What word do you get?
review.why: Take off /p/ and put on /f/. P-in becomes f-in.
